record.original_question: For three-dimensional isotropic elastic polycrystals obtained by combining differently oriented grains of a single crystal, what pairs (kappa*,mu*) of effective bulk and shear moduli are achievable? In particular, can one characterize the full feasible region beyond the currently sharp bulk-modulus bounds and the known but non-optimal shear-modulus bounds?

evidence.quote: Problem 13: What are the possible (κ∗, µ∗)-pairs for three-dimensional isotropic elastic polycrystals (composites built from a single crystal in various orientations)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider three-dimensional linearly elastic polycrystals: composite materials assembled from grains that are all copies of a single anisotropic crystal, where the grains differ only by rigid rotations of the crystal's elasticity tensor. Assume the grain geometry is such that the resulting composite is macroscopically (statistically) isotropic, so that its effective elasticity tensor is described by an effective bulk modulus κ* and an effective shear modulus μ*.

Given the elasticity tensor of a fixed single crystal, determine the set
G = { (κ*, μ*) ∈ ℝ_{>0} × ℝ_{>0} : (κ*, μ*) is realizable as the pair of effective bulk and shear moduli of some macroscopically isotropic 3D polycrystal built from rotated copies of the given crystal }.

Specifically: characterize G completely. The known sharp bounds on κ* alone, together with the known (but not generally optimal) bounds on μ*, confine G to a rectangle in the (κ*, μ*)-plane; the task is to determine the precise feasible region within (or strictly inside) this rectangle, and to exhibit microgeometries attaining each point of the boundary.
artifact.status_search_result: In the planar (2D) case, a complete characterization of the achievable (κ*, μ*) pairs for polycrystals built from a single crystal was obtained by Avellaneda–Cherkaev–Gibiansky–Milton–Rudelson and refined in subsequent works (including extremal planar polycrystal constructions published in 2021). In three dimensions, the bulk-modulus bounds are sharp but the shear-modulus bounds are generally not optimal, and no complete characterization of the feasible (κ*, μ*) region appears in the literature; recent works (e.g., on Hashin–Shtrikman bounds for 3D polycrystals of arbitrary symmetry) only provide bounds, not a full characterization. The problem is thus still open in 3D.

status_evidence.title: Planar polycrystals with extremal bulk and shear moduli
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of planar polycrystals attaining extremal bulk and shear moduli, building on the complete 2D characterization.
status_evidence.claim: The 2D analog has been completely characterized and refined, while 3D constructions attaining the bounds remain elusive.

status_evidence.title: A complete characterization of the possible bulk and shear moduli of planar polycrystals
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a complete characterization for planar (2D) polycrystals built from a single crystal in various orientations.
status_evidence.claim: The planar version is solved; the 3D version is the natural remaining question.

status_evidence.title: Determination of Hashin–Shtrikman bounds on the isotropic effective elastic moduli of polycrystals of any symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Computes Hashin–Shtrikman bounds for 3D polycrystals of arbitrary symmetry, but these bounds are not generally attained for the shear modulus.
status_evidence.claim: Current 3D results give bounds but not a sharp characterization of the (κ*,μ*) region.
